quote: the amendments made by this title shall take effect upon the expiration of the 30-day period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, and shall apply to any action or prosecution commenced on or after such effective date.
why: Sec. 105 makes the Title I amendments (secs. 103-104 amending 1446) apply only to actions commenced on or after the effective date 30 days after the Dec. 7, 2011 enactment, with removed cases dated by their state-court commencement.

quote: this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect on the earlier of-- (1) the date of enactment of this Act; or (2) the date of the enactment of the Act entitled ``An Act to provide for the continuation of agricultural programs through fiscal year 2012, and for other purposes'' (H.R. 2419
why: Sec. 4(b) makes the amendments by secs. 14001, 14004 and 14005 effective on the enactment of H.R. 2419 (Pub. L. 110-234, May 22, 2008), earlier than this Act's June 18, 2008 enactment.

No effective-date provision covers the secs. 101-103 amendments to 12 U.S.C. 1759 (only a grandfather of existing members and a filing-date scope rule for new subsection (g)), so they take effect on approval, Aug. 7, 1998.
The amendments to section 1817 by secs. 736(a)(5)-(6), 801(d)(1) and 900(e)(1)(D) carry no effective-date provision, so they take effect on approval, Dec. 8, 2003.
Sec. 601(b)(3) striking the FCC from Clayton Act sec. 7 has no timing provision, so it takes effect on approval, Feb. 8, 1996.
Sec. 136 of the Interior appropriations division amending 16 U.S.C. 1011(a) has no timing provision, so it takes effect on approval, Oct. 21, 1998.
Sec. 508 adding 18 U.S.C. 2422(b) has no timing provision, so it takes effect on approval, Feb. 8, 1996.
Sec. 112 amending section 1584 has no effective-date or applicability provision, so it takes effect on approval, Oct. 28, 2000.
Sec. 602 amending 12 U.S.C. 1422 is not covered by any Title VI effective-date provision (only sec. 607 has one), so it takes effect on approval, Nov. 12, 1999.

quote: The amendment made by this section shall be effective as if included in the enactment of section 381 of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (Public Law 104-193; 110 Stat. 2257).
why: Sec. 5612(b) makes its 1169(a)(2)(B) amendment effective as if included in PRWORA sec. 381 (Aug. 22, 1996), while secs. 5611 and 5613 apply only to medical child support orders issued on or after the Aug. 5, 1997 enactment.
